title: The long way east
text: Three road trips in five weeks and the group is flat. The high-performance staff want to cut Tuesday's main session to rest the legs before another four-hour flight.

choices.label: Cut the session
choices.result: The legs get a break. The week's main session goes.

choices.label: Train as planned
choices.result: The work is banked. The group boards the plane tired.

title: Stay east or fly home?
text: Back-to-back games in Melbourne. The club can base the squad in a Melbourne hotel for the week, or fly everyone home to their families and back again.

choices.label: Base the squad in Melbourne

effects.why: The squad spent a week on the road together

choices.result: A week of hotel rooms and team dinners. The families miss them.

choices.label: Fly home midweek
choices.result: A few nights at home, and two more flights.

title: Homesick in Perth
text: {name}, drafted from interstate, has gone quiet. His host family says he's ringing home every night and talking about the other side of the Nullarbor.

choices.label: Send him home for a week

effects.why: You let him go home when he needed it
The senior players noticed the special treatment

choices.result: {first} goes home for a week. The senior group notices.

choices.label: Keep him busy here

effects.why: The club held the line with a homesick kid

hit.why: He asked about a trade home

effects.hit_result: He's asking about a trade home at season's end.

choices.result: Training, more training, and dinner with the host family.

choices.label: Fly his family over

effects.why: The club brought his family to him

choices.result: His mum and dad land on Friday. The club pays the fares.

title: Bring him home
text: A West Australian at a Victorian club has told his manager he wants to come home. His club is asking for a first-round pick.

choices.label: Pay the price

effects.why: A West Australian came home to play

choices.result: A proven player who wants to be here. The first-round pick goes east.

choices.label: Wait until his contract runs out

effects.why: The club held to its draft plan

effects.hit_result: Another club got him first, and the press called you timid.

choices.result: You keep the pick and wait.

title: Local or the best on the board?
text: At your pick, the best player left is a Victorian. Two spots lower is a West Australian the recruiters rate nearly as highly, and he'll never ask to go home.

choices.label: Take the best available

effects.why: The club took the best player on the board

effects.hit_result: Within a few seasons he asked to go home.

choices.result: The higher-rated kid pulls on the jumper.

choices.label: Take the local

effects.why: The club passed on the best player left

choices.result: The WA football community approves. The rated kid goes elsewhere.

title: Derby week
text: Western Derby week. The whole state has an opinion, and every workplace in Perth is split between blue and gold and purple.

choices.label: Lean into it

effects.hit_result: A player's comment ended up on the back page.

choices.result: Training is ferocious all week.

choices.label: Treat it like any other week

effects.why: The group kept to its own routine in derby week

choices.result: Business as usual. The supporters think you've gone soft.

title: Derby week after a loss
text: You're coming off a loss into derby week and talkback is brutal. The club's biggest members' group wants the coach at their function on Thursday night.

choices.label: Front the members
choices.result: The members feel heard. The players hear their coach spent the night out.

choices.label: Send the football manager
choices.result: The review stays on track. The members wanted the coach.

title: The waiting list
text: Thousands are waiting for a reserved seat. Marketing wants to sell more memberships without seats; the long-time members say it cheapens the badge.

choices.label: Open more memberships

effects.why: Long-time members feel the badge was cheapened

choices.result: Money comes in. The old guard grumble.

choices.label: Keep the list

effects.why: Long-time members kept their exclusive badge

choices.result: The badge stays exclusive. Revenue is left on the table.

title: The owners want their share
text: The club is owned by the state's football commission, and a good year means a surplus. The commission wants more of it sent to grassroots footy; the football department wants it spent on staff.

choices.label: Send it to the grassroots
choices.result: Country clubs get the money. No new development coach this year.

choices.label: Spend it on the football department
choices.result: A new development coach starts Monday. The commission remembers.

title: Community camp
text: The preseason community camp heads to a country town: the Goldfields, the Pilbara or the South West. The whole list could go, or just the leadership group.

choices.label: Take the whole list

effects.why: The whole list spent three days in the country together

choices.result: Three days of school visits and country hospitality. Three days off the track.

choices.label: Send the leaders only
choices.result: The training is banked. The town feels short-changed.

title: A home game in the country
text: The state government offers money to move a home game to a ground in the South West. It would sell out, but the ground is small and the players don't know it.

choices.label: Take the game south
choices.result: A sell-out in the South West. The city members lose a game.

choices.label: Keep it at home

effects.why: The city members kept their home game

choices.result: The home ground stays home. The government and the regions are unimpressed.

title: Perth heat
text: It's forecast to pass 38 degrees all week. The sports scientists want sessions moved to 6am; the senior players say the heat is part of being a Perth side.

choices.label: Train at dawn
choices.result: Alarms at 4:30. The legs stay good.

choices.label: Train in the heat

effects.why: The group trained through a Perth scorcher

choices.result: Hard work in the heat. The physios are busy.

title: The early start
text: The broadcaster wants your home games to start earlier so they land in east-coast prime time. In Perth that means a rush from work for families and more footy in the afternoon heat.

choices.label: Agree

effects.why: Working families miss the start

choices.result: The broadcaster is happy. Half the crowd arrives at quarter time.

choices.label: Push back

effects.why: Members saw the club stand up for them

choices.result: The members back you. The league and the broadcaster remember.

title: Flat-track bullies
text: An eastern-states panel show calls your side flat-track bullies: unbeatable at home, soft on the road. The players have seen it.

choices.label: Bite back on air
choices.result: The clip goes around. Lose on the road and they'll play it again.

choices.label: Say nothing; pin it up

effects.why: The group let its footy do the answering

choices.result: It's on the wall in the rooms. Training is fired up.

title: Finals or failure
text: A big, rich club with a full stadium expects September. The chairman says privately that missing finals this year won't be acceptable.

choices.label: Accept the target
choices.result: The board is happy for now. Every loss counts against the target.

choices.label: Talk the board down
choices.result: No hard target for the players to carry. The press reads it as excuses.

title: Rebuild or reload?
text: The members are restless, the senior players are ageing, and the club must decide: rebuild through the draft, or trade for experienced players now.

choices.label: Rebuild

effects.why: The club backed its kids to win the next flag

choices.result: The young players will get games. The members brace for pain.

choices.label: Reload
choices.result: Experienced players come in. The young blokes see their games disappear.

title: A whisper from the nightclubs
text: Security staff have heard the club's name mentioned around a nightclub crowd with a drug problem. Nothing is proven, and the leaders say the group is fine.

choices.label: Crack down now

effects.why: The club acted before anything was proven

choices.result: Testing, curfews and hard talks. The leaders feel mistrusted.

choices.label: Trust the leaders

effects.why: The leaders were trusted to look after the group

hit.why: It became a scandal the club had been warned about

effects.hit_result: Later in the season it became a scandal.

choices.result: The leaders own it. The club waits and hopes.

title: Trouble on a night out
text: One of the players was in a scuffle outside a Northbridge venue after the weekend's game. Police took no action, but the footage is all over social media.

choices.label: Suspend him for a week

effects.why: The club stood a player down over his conduct

choices.result: He sits out a game. The side is a man short of its best.

choices.label: Deal with it internally
choices.result: He plays. The press says the club hasn't learnt.

title: The Swans again
text: Sydney this week. These two clubs have a habit of finishing within a kick of each other, and the senior players talk about it.

choices.label: Drill the last five minutes
choices.result: A week of close-game work. The legs feel it.

choices.label: Keep it light
choices.result: An easy week. The group runs out fresh.

title: The Magpie army
text: Collingwood this week, in front of a huge, one-eyed crowd. The young players have never heard noise like it.

choices.label: Pump crowd noise into training
choices.result: Speakers blare at training. The senior players roll their eyes.

choices.label: Tell them to enjoy it
choices.result: The kids are told to soak it up. The first ten minutes will tell.

title: The next big ruck
text: This club has a proud line of big, athletic ruckmen. The young ruck is raw, but the members are already calling him the next one.

choices.label: Play him now

effects.hit_result: He was beaten badly in the ruck, and the side felt it.

choices.result: The members cheer his first hit-out.

choices.label: Another month in the reserves
choices.result: He learns his craft in the twos. The members grumble.

title: The backline wall
text: The defenders take pride in reading the play and taking intercept marks. The forwards say the backs are too slow to push up and start the attack.

choices.label: Back the defenders

effects.why: The backline was backed for what it does best
The forwards want more drive from behind

choices.result: The backs walk taller. The forwards keep grumbling.

choices.label: Ask them to push up

effects.why: The defence was asked to attack too

choices.result: The backs push up. They feel their strength is being taken away.

title: North to the Kimberley
text: The recruiters want a week in the Kimberley and the Pilbara watching junior and country footy, and the club's Indigenous players want to go with them.

choices.label: Fund the trip

effects.why: The club went north with its Indigenous players

effects.hit_result: The trip turned up a prospect for next year's draft.

choices.result: A week of red dirt and country footy.

choices.label: Watch the vision from Perth

effects.why: The communities noticed the club didn't come

choices.result: The money stays in Perth. The communities up north notice.

title: A son of the club
text: The son of a former Eagle is old enough for the draft and wants to play for his dad's club. Other recruiters rate him, so he won't come cheap.

choices.label: Take him

effects.why: A pick went on a name, not the best player left

choices.result: The family is in tears. A pick goes that could have gone elsewhere.

choices.label: Let him go

effects.why: The club took the best player on its board

choices.result: A club family is left disappointed. The pick stays.

title: Reunion week
text: An old Eagles side is holding its reunion at the club, and one of its greats offers to speak to the players on Thursday night.

choices.label: Have him speak

effects.why: A great told the group what winning feels like

choices.result: The room hangs on every word. It's a late night before the game.

choices.label: Keep the week normal

effects.why: The week stayed about this game

choices.result: Preparation stays untouched. The old boys feel snubbed.

title: Open training
text: Thousands of kids are on school holidays, and marketing wants an open session with signing time afterwards.

choices.label: Open the gates
choices.result: The kids flood in. The session is lighter than planned.

choices.label: Keep it closed
choices.result: A full session. The club looks distant.
